# Environment tools

Read `ENVIRONMENT.json` for the site's policy, adapter composition and enforced constraints, and `tasks.json`
for task details. `STATUS.json` contains the latest budget, loaded stack, adapters and running job IDs.

running train its completed steps, latest mean reward and GPU-hours so far, as the site reports them. `tasks/<task>/eval_prompt.txt` (when
the site provides it) is the prompt the policy receives at evaluation; training prompts are checked against it. `tasks/INDEX.md` lists each task's goal line, dev and

| --- | --- |
| `python3 train.py SPEC` | Submit JSON/YAML spec to the installed trainer; see `skills/trainer/SKILL.md`. |
| `python3 eval.py --adapter A[,B...]\|base\|loaded --task T --seeds N` | Evaluate on the next N unused dev seeds (the result lists them; the base column has its own) with the task's `tasks/<task>/eval_prompt.txt` verbatim (no training `note`/`goal`; the final score uses the same prompt). Results are written only when all seeds finish, so an eval that reaches its time limit usually fails with no count (rarely: a count over the seeds that finished, with `partial`). Where the site can resume an eval (eval port dq-t1v2), an eval stopped by the cluster (time limit, preemption, node failure) continues its remaining seeds in a new Slurm job, at most 3 times; its status then says `continued from seed k in job J`, and its result lists every Slurm job (`jobs`) and each continuation (`continued`: `job` stopped, `cause`, `from` seed, `of` seeds, `continued_in` job), as it lists site retries. |
| `python3 load.py load A [B...]` | Replace the loaded stack (names separated by spaces; eval.py separates them by commas). |
| `python3 load.py stack A [B...]` | Append to the loaded stack. |
| `python3 load.py unload [A...]` | Remove names, or return to base with no names. |
| `python3 status.py [ID...]` | Read job states and results; no IDs shows all jobs. The last line states what finishing now would score. |
| `python3 wait.py all\|ID... [--max 4h\|90m]` | Submit a wait barrier: your next turn starts when those jobs finish or after `--max` (default 2h), whichever comes first. """Shared by train.py, eval.py, load.py, wait.py, cancel.py, finish.py: write one request file to jobs/; the environment picks it up when

JOBS = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "jobs")


def submit(kind, args):

    n = 1
    while True:

    with f:
